mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let’s bring it all together with a few things worth carrying forward. First, remember—adaptability and a sense of humor aren’t just nice to have. They’re how you survive, and sometimes even thrive, when life gets tough. Language can do more than just communicate—it can break down barriers and open doors you never thought you’d get through. And let’s not forget: the love and strength of family, especially a mother’s love, can light even the darkest paths. Forgiving someone isn’t about letting them off the hook—it’s about freeing yourself, finding your own peace. Most importantly, real belonging happens when you accept yourself, not when you’re squeezing into someone else’s idea of who you should be. So, here’s what this means for you. If you hold onto just one thing, let it be the quiet courage to choose hope, even when things feel impossible. Life’s going to throw contradictions, losses, and moments that don’t seem fair your way. But as Trevor’s journey reminds us, you’re not defined by what happens to you—you’re defined by how you choose to respond. Lean into your own story. Use your voice, your humor, and your resilience to build bridges and claim your place in this world. Even if the path ahead feels unclear, you always have the power to choose—to move forward, to forgive, and to create something new. The world might not always make sense, but the choices you make can bring meaning, connection, and a whole lot of hope.
